html:
Center-pivot irrigation is a way of watering fields with a long line of sprinklers that turns slowly around a central well, like the hand of a clock. It leaves the green circles that you see from a plane over dry farm country.

A Nebraska farmer, Frank Zybach, invented it in the late 1940s and patented it in 1952. Companies such as Valmont improved and sold it. One machine could water a whole field with little labour, even on rolling land.

It changed the Great Plains of the United States, the land of the Dust Bowl. From the 1960s farmers pumped water from the vast Ogallala Aquifer to grow corn, soybeans and wheat where only grass or dry farming had worked before.

The cost is the water itself. The aquifer fills very slowly, and in parts of Kansas and Texas it has dropped so far that wells have run dry. The same machines spread to Saudi Arabia, Libya and other dry lands, where they also draw on ancient groundwater. Along with new seeds and fertiliser, they were part of the wider Green Revolution in farming.
sum: Center-pivot irrigation is a way of watering fields with a long line of sprinklers that turns slowly around a central well, like the hand of a clock. It leaves the green circles that you see from a plane over dry farm country.
